LESSON: READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.8: Reading for Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading for Comprehension, part of Reading in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you show love to your family members? 2. How does vocabulary help in language acquisition?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. pick out target vocabulary from a reading text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. infer meaning of words from context,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. pick out target vocabulary from a reading text,

   Reading for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. infer meaning of words from context,

   Reading for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition.

   Reading for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to conduct a reading session on texts related to the theme,

2. team up to pick out thematic vocabulary from the text,

3. build a vocabulary bank of words identified,

4. collaborate to infer meaning of vocabulary from context,

5. work with peers to match meaning of words to the respective words,

6. take turns to make sentences using the vocabulary. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to conduct a reading session on texts related to the theme,
2. team up to pick out thematic vocabulary from the text,
3. build a vocabulary bank of words identified,
4. collaborate to infer meaning of vocabulary from context,
5. work with peers to match meaning of words to the respective words,
6. take turns to make sentences using the vocabulary. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading for Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner contributes to group decision making when taking turns to make sentences using

vocabulary.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: This is promoted as the learner explores views when working with peers to match

meaning of words to the respective words.
